source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: How does Nurse Ana give BCG?
questions.rationale: BCG for infants is 0.05 mL intradermal in the right deltoid region.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)
questions.quote: BCG 0.05 mL ID Right deltoid region

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: Where does Nurse Ana inject the hepatitis B vaccine for an infant?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis B and DPT-containing vaccines are 0.5 mL IM in the upper outer thigh (vastus lateralis).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)
questions.quote: HEPA B 0.5 mL IM Upper outer portion of thigh (Vastus lateralis)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: By which route does Nurse Ana give the measles-containing vaccine?
questions.rationale: Measles vaccine is 0.5 mL subcutaneous in the outer upper arm.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)
questions.quote: MEASLES 0.5 mL SQ Outer portion of upper arm

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: What is the minimum interval between pentavalent doses?
questions.rationale: Pentavalent starts at 6 weeks, with 3 doses at 4-week intervals. Shorter intervals may lessen the antibody response.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)
questions.quote: Pentavalent 6 weeks 3 4 weeks

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which three micronutrient deficiencies does the DOH nutrition program target?
questions.rationale: The common nutritional deficiencies addressed are vitamin A, iron, and iodine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nutrition Program (PDF p. 93)
questions.quote: Common Nutritional Deficiencies

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Applying pit and fissure sealant to a child's molars is which type of oral intervention?
questions.rationale: Preventive oral interventions include oral exams, oral hygiene, pit and fissure sealant, and fluoride use. Fillings and extractions are curative.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Health Program (PDF p. 93)
questions.quote: Pit & Fissure Sealant Program

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Barangay San Isidro has scattered houses. The PHN is reviewing the water supply.
questions.stem: The barangay uses a protected well with no distribution system. What level of water facility is this?
questions.rationale: Level I (point source) is a protected well or developed spring without a distribution system, suited to rural areas with scattered houses.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Water Supply Facilities (PDF p. 94)
questions.quote: Protect well or developed spring with an outlet but without a distribution system

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Barangay San Isidro has scattered houses. The PHN is reviewing the water supply.
questions.stem: The farthest Level I user should be no more than how far from the source?
questions.rationale: A Level I source serves 15 to 25 households, and the farthest user must be no more than 250 meters away.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Water Supply Facilities (PDF p. 94)
questions.quote: Outreach must not be more than 250 meters from the farthest user

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A water system with a reservoir, piped network, and communal faucets for 4 to 6 households each is which level?
questions.rationale: Level II (communal faucet system) has a piped network and communal faucets, with one faucet per 4 to 6 households and no more than 25 meters from the farthest house.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Water Supply Facilities (PDF p. 94)
questions.quote: One faucet per 4 to 6 households

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which water source is UNAPPROVED?
questions.rationale: Unapproved water facilities include open dug wells, unimproved springs, and wells that need priming.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Unapproved Water Facility (PDF p. 94)
questions.quote: Unimproved springs

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: When must a water supply source be disinfected?
questions.rationale: Disinfection is required for newly constructed water supply facilities and for facilities that have been repaired or improved.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Water Quality Surveillance (PDF p. 95)
questions.quote: Newly constructed water supply facilities

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A household uses a pour-flush toilet. What level of toilet facility is this?
questions.rationale: Level I includes non-water carriage facilities (pit latrines, reed odorless earth closets) and those needing small amounts of water (pour-flush toilets, aqua privies).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Toilet Facilities (PDF p. 95)
questions.quote: Toilet Facilities requiring small amount of water

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which law is the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines?
questions.rationale: PD 856 is the Sanitation Code. RA 9003 is Ecological Solid Waste Management, RA 9275 is the Clean Water Act, and RA 8749 is the Clean Air Act.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Health and Sanitation Laws (PDF p. 94)
questions.quote: PD 856 – Sanitation Code of the Philippines

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A barangay starts waste segregation and a materials recovery facility. Which law mandates this?
questions.rationale: RA 9003, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, governs solid waste management, including segregation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Health and Sanitation Laws (PDF p. 94)
questions.quote: RA 9003- Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under DOH AO 1-2006, which stool test is required for food handlers?
questions.rationale: DOH AO 1-2006 requires laboratories to use the formalin ether concentration technique (FECT) instead of direct fecal smear for food handlers' stool analysis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Food Sanitation Program (PDF p. 95)
questions.quote: Formalin Ether Concentration Technique (FECT) instead of the direct fecal smear

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In teaching food safety, to what temperature should all parts of cooked or reheated food reach?
questions.rationale: Food should be cooked thoroughly so all parts reach 70°C, and reheated to at least 70°C.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Four Rights in Food Safety (PDF p. 96)
questions.quote: Cook food thoroughly (temperature on all parts of the food should reach 70 degrees centigrade

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How long can cooked food stay at room temperature?
questions.rationale: Under right storage, cooked food should be left at room temperature for no more than 2 hours. 'When in doubt, throw it out!'
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Four Rights in Food Safety (PDF p. 96)
questions.quote: All cooked food should be left at room temperature for not more than two hours

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which teaching belongs to 'right source' in the four rights of food safety?
options: Keep raw and cooked food apart
questions.rationale: Right source includes buying fresh food, checking expiry dates, avoiding dented or bulging cans, and boiling water for at least 2 minutes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Four Rights in Food Safety (PDF p. 95)
questions.quote: Avoid buying canned goods with dents, bulges, deformation, broken seals and improper seams

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: How long is a Sentrong Sigla certification valid?
questions.rationale: Sentrong Sigla certification is valid for 2 years. Facilities that keep their status get renewal stickers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sentrong Sigla Certification (PDF p. 96)
questions.quote: The SS Certification validity of certification is every two years.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In what kind of pot should herbal decoctions be boiled?
questions.rationale: Medicinal plants are boiled in enamelware or clay pots, not aluminum, and the pots are cleaned well before and after.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine Guidelines (PDF p. 97)
questions.quote: In boiling the plants, use enamel were or clay pots, not aluminum ware.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A mother has given an herbal remedy 3 times with no improvement. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: If there is no improvement after two or three doses, the client should consult a physician. Only one plant is used at a time.
explanations: Use one plant at a time.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine Guidelines (PDF p. 97)
questions.quote: If there are no signs of improvement after two or three administration of the drug, consult a physician

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How many tablespoons of FRESH lagundi leaves are boiled for a 9-year-old with cough?
questions.rationale: For lagundi, fresh leaves are 6 tbsp for adults, 3 tbsp for ages 7–12, and 1½ tbsp for ages 2–6. Boil in 2 cups of water for 15 minutes and divide into 3 doses.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lagundi (PDF p. 97)
questions.quote: 7- 12 y/o 3 tbsp. 2 tbsp.
